title: Vivaldi, Spring, first movement, in two recordings
work: The Four Seasons · Spring, RV 269 — I. Allegro
question: How do the solo violin’s birdsong passages and the orchestral ritornello differ between these two performances?
intro: Vivaldi’s Spring opens in E major with a refrain for the strings. Bird calls interrupt it, then a storm, and the refrain returns between these episodes. John Harrison recorded it live with the Wichita State University Chamber Players in 2000; the second performance comes from Musopen.

recordings.label: John Harrison · Wichita State University Chamber Players · Robert Turizziani
recordings.note: Harrison’s live, unedited performance at Wiedemann Recital Hall, Wichita State University, on 6 February 2000.

recordings.label: Modena Chamber Orchestra
recordings.note: A solo violin and chamber orchestra, issued by Musopen as part of The Four Seasons.

passages.label: Opening ritornello in E major
passages.note: The strings open with short, repeated phrases in E major that represent the arrival of spring.

passages.label: Birdsong episode, violins
passages.note: The violins trade trills and short rising and falling calls, with rests between one call and the next.

passages.label: Second phrase of the ritornello
passages.note: Only the second phrase of the refrain returns, and the orchestra takes over the violin calls heard before it.

passages.label: Storm episode
passages.note: Rapid violin figures break into the refrain; during the storm the music moves through B major towards C♯ minor.

passages.label: Ritornello from C♯ minor to E major
passages.note: The refrain starts in C♯ minor and moves back to E major, where the strings play the opening tune again.

passages.label: Final ritornello in E major
passages.note: The orchestra brings back the refrain in E major after the solo violin’s last passages.
